items.prompt: A VIEWER tries to open someone else's notification, which has a SENT delivery. What comes back?
items.answer: 404 "Notification not found.", the same as for a missing id
distractors: 403 Forbidden, because the viewer is not that notification's recipient
409, because only the recipient may move it to opened
200 with opened: true, as the delivery has been sent
items.explanation: Without notifications:view:any, a recipient mismatch throws ApiError(404, "Notification not found.") with the same message as a missing record, so a guessed id reveals nothing.

items.prompt: A VIEWER opens their own notification whose only delivery is already OPENED. What is the result?
items.answer: 409 "Only sent notifications can transition to opened."
distractors: 200 with opened: true, since a repeat open is idempotent
404, since an opened notification is hidden from the list
200, and the openedAt timestamp moves to the current time
items.explanation: Only SENT deliveries are eligible; with none, sentDeliveryIds is empty and the service throws 409. Repeated opens are not idempotent successes.

items.prompt: An OPERATOR opens another user's notification that has a SENT delivery. What happens?
items.answer: It succeeds, as OPERATOR holds notifications:view:any
distractors: 404, because only the recipient can ever open it
403, as OPERATOR lacks the notifications:open:own action
409, because staff opens are blocked by the lifecycle check
items.explanation: OPERATOR has notifications:view:any, so the recipient comparison is skipped, the SENT check passes, and the open is recorded. The guide flags that staff can inflate open metrics this way.

items.answer: COMPLETED, as the completed check runs first
distractors: FAILED, as SKIPPED is in the failed set
QUEUED, as nothing was actually delivered
PARTIAL_FAILURE, as nothing was sent
items.explanation: SKIPPED is in both completedStatuses and failedStatuses. The allCompleted check comes first, so an all-skipped notification (opt-outs) is COMPLETED.

items.answer: QUEUED, so a partly delivered notification looks unsent
distractors: PROCESSING, as one of the deliveries is still pending
PARTIAL_FAILURE; only part of it has been delivered
COMPLETED, since one delivery has already reached SENT
items.explanation: Not all completed, not all failed, and no FAILED status, so no PARTIAL_FAILURE; with no PROCESSING delivery the fallback is QUEUED. The review calls this a regression to QUEUED.

items.prompt: Every notification in a batch is PARTIAL_FAILURE. What does deriveBatchStatus return?
items.answer: QUEUED, since no branch matches without a COMPLETED one
distractors: PARTIAL_FAILURE, the same status every notification has
FAILED, as none of the notifications fully completed
PROCESSING, since the batch has not finished delivering
items.explanation: The PARTIAL_FAILURE branch needs at least one COMPLETED notification; all-COMPLETED and all-FAILED do not match either, and with no PROCESSING the fallback is QUEUED. The review lists it as a real mislabel.

items.prompt: updateNotificationStatus throws during an open. Which writes have already happened?
items.answer: The delivery open and openedAt; no batch status and no audit
distractors: None, as the whole open runs inside a single transaction
All of them except the audit row, which is written last
Only the audit row, which is recorded before any of the updates
items.explanation: There is no transaction around lines 306-318. markDeliveryOpened and updateNotificationOpenedAt ran first; the error stops refresh before updateBatchStatus and createAuditLog. Lab case 6 pins exactly this.

items.prompt: A user's rate-limit window is already full (sentCount equals limit). What does the next check return?
items.answer: allowed: true, because sentCount stays equal to limit
distractors: allowed: false, with nextAvailableAt set to the next window
allowed: false, because the upsert pushes sentCount past it
An error, since the CASE refuses to update a full window
items.explanation: The CASE keeps sentCount at limit when full, and allowed is sentCount <= limit, which is still true. The limiter never denies, so the RATE_LIMITED branch in the worker is unreachable.

items.prompt: markDeliveryOpened repeats status = SENT in its updateMany where clause. Why, if the service already filtered?
items.answer: A delivery can change state between the read and the write
distractors: Prisma refuses an updateMany that has no status in it at all
It also opens the QUEUED deliveries that share the same ids
The service filter runs for VIEWERs only; admins skip it
items.explanation: The service reads deliveries at line 286 and writes at 306. Repeating the SENT predicate in SQL protects against a delivery leaving SENT in between.

items.prompt: A worker crashes after claiming a delivery (status PROCESSING). Will another worker reclaim it once its lock goes stale?
items.answer: No, as the claim only selects QUEUED, RETRYING or RATE_LIMITED
distractors: Yes, as soon as lockedAt is older than the lock timeout
Yes, on the next run of the worker's startup cleanup job
No, because SKIP LOCKED hides it from every later claim
items.explanation: The stale-lease test (lockedAt < staleBefore) sits inside a WHERE that excludes PROCESSING, so a crashed worker's delivery is stranded. SKIP LOCKED only skips rows locked by an open transaction.

items.prompt: How does refreshNotificationAndBatchState update the batch after an open?
items.answer: It re-derives the batch status from all its notification statuses
distractors: It adds one to the batch's opened counter for the new open
It copies the notification's new status onto the batch row
It leaves the batch untouched until the worker's next polling run
items.explanation: It reads every delivery status of the notification, derives and writes the notification status, then reads every notification status of the batch and derives the batch status: recomputed from scratch, never incremented.

items.prompt: A VIEWER sends an open for a notification id that does not exist. Which line decides the outcome?
items.answer: Line 288: the null record throws a 404 Notification not found
distractors: Line 284: requireAction rejects the call before any lookup runs
Line 294: the recipient check throws its 404 for the viewer
Line 302: an empty delivery list throws the 409 conflict
items.explanation: VIEWER holds notifications:open:own, so requireAction passes; findNotificationDetail returns null and the `if (!notification)` branch at 288-289 throws 404 before ownership or lifecycle are checked.

items.front: The four concerns in markNotificationOpenedForSession, in order
items.back: Ownership (292-296, 404 unless view:any or recipient); lifecycle (298-304, 409 unless a SENT delivery; repeated in SQL); aggregation (308 -> refresh at 57-71); audit (310-318). No transaction wraps the writes.

No deliveries -> QUEUED; all in {SENT, OPENED, SKIPPED} -> COMPLETED; all in {FAILED, SKIPPED} -> FAILED; some delivered and some FAILED -> PARTIAL_FAILURE; else PROCESSING if any PROCESSING, otherwise QUEUED.

items.front: Why transient delivery failures retry forever
items.back: markDeliveryDeferred never increments attemptCount, so nextAttemptCount is always 1, exhausted never becomes true and backoff stays at one minute. Fix: increment attemptCount for RETRYING (not RATE_LIMITED).
